items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: Oh man, well Philly Joe really and “Billy Boy” man... And Art Blakey man, in the very beginning Art Blakey was just thundering.

ctx.x: Was it, there’s a live thing you did —

Oh yeah, Antibes. Yeah, yeah. That’s right. We didn’t get paid for that for a long time. Yeah we did that and that’s about it, but Woody was a great experience for me. See that’s another thing, when I got off of Woody’s band and I came to New York let’s get that guy that was with Woody. That’s the way it went man. It just does. They hear you, they’re playing a Woody Herman record on the radio locally on the jazz station. Other musicians hear it and — I was getting gigs just because I was with Woody. Actually I…

because I’m not playing that kind of music that much. You know when the drummer sneaks in? You know when you’re playing and you sneak in soft-soft-soft-soft. He never heard that man. He flipped over it. And after a while he’d go, [whispers] “Sneak in, sneak in,” you know while he’s on stage. You know I wouldn’t be playing and he’d go “Sneak in, sneak in, man, sneak in.” And then just soft cymbal, just soft cymbal, and even no hi- hat man. Then all of a sudden a little hi-hat, maybe cross stick you know. He went…
